description: Taking these together increases the risk of serious bleeding.
Ibuprofen with warfarin increases the risk of serious bleeding, including in the stomach.
Naproxen with warfarin increases the risk of serious bleeding, including in the stomach.
Using two blood-thinning medicines together increases the risk of serious bleeding.
Clarithromycin greatly raises simvastatin levels, increasing the risk of severe muscle damage.
Clarithromycin raises atorvastatin levels, which can increase the risk of muscle side effects.
Both medicines can raise potassium; together they can cause dangerously high potassium levels.
Ibuprofen can weaken the blood-pressure-lowering effect of lisinopril, and together they can harm the kidneys.
Naproxen can weaken the blood-pressure-lowering effect of lisinopril, and together they can harm the kidneys.
Omeprazole can reduce how well clopidogrel is activated in the body, which may make it less effective.
Metoclopramide blocks dopamine and can counteract levodopa, which may worsen Parkinson's symptoms.
Ibuprofen may interfere with the heart-protective effect of low-dose aspirin, and together they raise the risk of stomach bleeding.
Together these increase the risk of bleeding. They are often prescribed together on purpose, so discuss this with your doctor.
Ibuprofen can reduce the effect of furosemide and increase the risk of kidney problems.
These medicines have opposite effects on the same body signals, so each may work less well.
